name: Harley & Yvaine
core: A blade who craves gentleness and the ropes that teach her surrender, and a ritualist who turns that chaos into clarity through breath, rope and remembrance. Yvaine makes people real by refusing to forget them. Harley, who was built to be unremembered and trained to be unremarkable in her own death, took four arcs to believe she was allowed to ask for the rest of it — and then knelt for the answer.
architecture: Yvaine tops. Unambiguously, and the Archive had this wrong — Harley's v5 profile reads a natural top until rope appears, and that is retired. Harley is a bottom. She brats her way toward it, smirks wider the closer she gets to begging, and melts the instant the rope comes out. Yvaine guides her there through breath, precision, silence and deliberate ceremony, and never rushes any of it.
weddingNote: rope-themed, because of course it was. Harley had held the question since Arc 7
note: Four arcs between deciding and asking. A woman trained as a government ghost — who maps exits, monitors danger and rehearses loss — spent from Arc 7 to Arc 11 holding a question about a future. That delay is the whole character. The wedding was rope-themed, which surprised precisely nobody: they got married in the language they already spoke.

quotes.line: Tie me… or I'll haunt your bed forever.
quotes.when: Already kneeling when she said it, which rather settles the question of who tops.
